analysis.title: The Bullion Report / Rieder On Rates / French Consumer Confidence / UK Inflation & Wages
key_insights: Gold: clients are structurally bullish but tactically cautious into year-end, focused on protecting P&L. Price is stuck in a low-conviction range with buying interest near $4,000/oz, and the tightening monetary-policy backdrop limits upside.
Structural gold support (geopolitical risk, de-dollarization, non-dollar settlement demand, central-bank buying) has not yet produced a catalyst strong enough to break the range.

Asian physical gold demand is strong, led by kilobar demand for mainland China. Buying began around the start of October, earlier than in recent years. Refinery slots and production orders are getting harder to secure, and some participants are transacting against renminbi rather than USD.

Rates: Rick Rieder says the 10y Treasury has taken a backseat to other fixed income opportunities, with about 7% available in short-dated single-A portfolios. AI-related issuance is pushing yields higher.

ETD Sales Trading sees the AI rally continuing, with IPOs announced and funding plentiful (chip financing deals for Space X and Broadcom). The better risk tone pushed fixed income futures lower. Rates only rally on equity weakness, and positioning is cleaner as shorts step back in.

French consumer confidence fell to 80 in October from 85 in September, versus a Bloomberg consensus of 85. It is the lowest since June 2013. The survey ran Sept. 25 to Oct. 19 and captured some of the social unrest in France.

UK BRC shop-price inflation rose to 2.1% y/y from 1.4% in October, the fastest since February 2024. BRC warns that 'the dam is starting to break' on cost pass-through after retailers absorbed costs for two years. Official CPI was 3.5% in September.

UK Chancellor is expected to announce a 3.9% National Living Wage rise to about GBP13.20 from GBP12.71, above 3.5% inflation. The under-21 rate would rise to about GBP11.27, ending the pledge to align it with the adult rate.

The EU is considering quotas or tariffs on Chinese chemicals, furniture and machinery as early as Q1 2027 to narrow a EUR360bn goods deficit. UBS WM CIO sees added trade friction and more dispersion, and forecasts 15% Eurozone earnings growth in both 2026 and 2027.

Israel election exit polls are due Tuesday 20:00 London. A bloc with 56-57+ seats and a 4-5 seat lead would reduce post-election uncertainty. The latest poll average has the Eizenkot camp at 53 seats and Netanyahu's at 51.

Rates Trading (Amar Mian): the market prices near-term Fed patience, but sticky inflation and AI capex skew terminal risks higher. The desk says to fade the recent 7y richening and expectations for cuts to long-end Treasury issuance.

Rates Trading (Sally Marshall): OATs are driving the market, with asset swaps strong on correlations. The long-end curve began flattening aggressively mid last week. The desk prefers basis wideners ahead of an event-heavy week.

US hedge funds cut AI exposure last week, with the strongest two-day reduction in Hyperscaler longs since covid before a reversal on Friday. Net exposure to AI is at the 17th percentile on a 1y lookback, raising short-squeeze risk on better earnings.

HSBC Q3: pre-tax profit $9.6bn, broadly in line. Pre-provision profit ex-notable items was 3% below consensus, impairments 21% below consensus, CET1 13.9% (20bp below consensus). A further buyback of up to $1bn was announced and FY26 guidance was retained.

RBNZ is all but certain to hike Wednesday from 2.75%. The desk expects a terminal rate near neutral (3-3.5%) and likes holding received 1y1y. Risks are positioning, the Nov. 7 election and the trade-weighted NZD.
FX Trading favors short AUDNZD into Wednesday's Australian CPI (30 minutes before the RBNZ decision), fading strength toward 1.2360-1.2370 with a wider stop above 1.2500.
Chile's central bank is likely to hold at 4.50% on Tuesday, and the focus is the easing tone. UBS forecasts 9.6% unemployment on Thursday.
FX Sales expects BRLMXN long unwinds to support MXN, while the fundamentals in Mexico are called abysmal. Banxico is likely to turn more hawkish or at least stop easing.
China industrial profits rose 14.4% y/y in September versus 4.2% in August. Profits for January-September rose 15.5%, with electronics up 103.8%.
EU and SSA spreads lagged the OAT tightening of almost 14bp. OATs are widening slightly in the London morning.
EUR vol softened after weeks of one-directional client buying. Skew rotation continues as the correlation between rates and implieds changes with OAT widening.
FX Trading: dollar strength is expected to extend into the Fed. It favors EURUSD and silver downside, sees gold heavy but cushioned by Asian reserve-manager buying, and sees USDJPY and USDCAD higher.

market_movers.rationale: UBS analyst Jason Napier sees a slightly softer underlying Q3 print. Weaker income was offset by better credit costs, and the focus will be on NII momentum, Wealth revenue and capital returns.

earnings_insights: HSBC Q3 2026: pre-tax profit $9.6bn, broadly in line with expectations (reported). Pre-provision profit ex-notable items 3% below consensus, revenue 2% light, banking NII 2% below consensus, fee and other income 1% lower. Impairments 21% below consensus, CET1 13.9% (20bp below consensus), Wealth profit 10% below UBS estimates.
HSBC announced another buyback of up to $1bn, maintained its $0.10 interim dividend, raised the expected Basel 3.1 benefit to 40-50bp, and retained FY26 guidance and targets through 2028.
AI-name earnings in the coming days could trigger a short squeeze given net AI positioning at the 17th percentile (Equity Sales view).
UBS WM CIO forecasts 15% Eurozone earnings growth in both 2026 and 2027.

tension_points.bear_case: Tightening monetary policy and tactical caution into year-end leave the price range-bound, and the FX desk sees gold heavy with dollar strength.
